name: House style
summary: Your one design package: your taste, learned from what you chose and rejected in Relay, Avex and Tally, on top of the fundamentals of interface design, with task guides for motion, unslopping, worst-case data, mobile web and variations, platform rules for GTK, Android, web and game UI, and a review checklist to run before calling UI work done.
description: Turn it on for any project with an interface. Every agent launched there gets three skills and the plugin's rules in its brief. house-style is your taste: clean and professional, near-black with one accent, nothing crowded, too round, too big, boxed, dated or AI-looking, one look across all your apps, and how you like to work (two or three real variations beside the before, one screen at a time, keep what you like, look at the render before reporting). It also holds the fundamentals (hierarchy, type, spacing, colour, measured contrast, controls, the seven states, copy, motion, data, icons), a ledger of named failures with fixes, your own words with dates behind each rule, and task guides merged from the design skills you used to install separately: motion (whether to animate, the values, gestures, performance, reduced motion, and review, audit, find and remove passes), unslopping an AI-looking screen and landing visuals (adapted from unslop, CC BY 4.0), worst-case data stress tests, web apps that feel native on a phone, React library picks and variations in code. house-style-native carries it onto GTK 4 desktop, Android with Compose, web pages, design-canvas mockups and game UI. house-style-review is the checklist and report format for a critique or a pass before done. A project's own design doc still wins for its exact tokens and settled decisions, and this plugin wins over generic design skills where they disagree.
